items.title: 67247_J.C. Higginbotham oral history interview
items.q: You remember Charlie Dixon? He was an arranger. He could arrange tunes and boy, the notes that he would put up on the blackboard, you had to do a whole lot of reading.

ctx.x: There's one more thing I wanted to ask you about and that was a little about what did you do in the Rhythm Club? You said they hung out there. What did they do when they were hanging out?

Just go in and say hello if you don't have no place to go. If you see guys sitting down playing cards, say may I get into and join, you know. Then sometimes they play poker and then they got a poolroom. They shoot pool, but no more music. They did have a blackboard there and the musicians would take their horns in there and one guy would write down something and see who could play it. That's when we were really having fun. Say, I bet you can't play this. You remember Charlie Dixon? He was an arranger. He could…
Were a lot of the musicians trying to learn to read better at that time?
